segmentation.text: or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph,
drive to a position parallel to, and
as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway
The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway
where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder.

The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The conduct the words require of it is carried by u4 and u1, not by the class.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning, which is not required.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role in {police_officer, ...}' read with role police_officer, governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph' refers to the paragraph's own provision that the driver 'shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows' listed vehicles 'to drive on the shoulder': the position this node requires excludes such a shoulder. st.shoulder 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute', read paved; dev.regulatory_sign 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... shoulder_use_permitted', governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or shoulder') that shoulder; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint.

'a position parallel to' the edge: the subject's heading (kin.heading 'direction the body points') is parallel, in either sense, to the designated direction (st.lane_direction 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of a travel region (st.travel_region) its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); the carrier's direction runs along its edge. st.travel_region's exclusion of the highway's extent is respected: it only selects the carrier the subject is on.

'clear of any intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) no st.intersection region ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line' is respected.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle moves with the subject ahead of it in its own frame, within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

the position is reached within a perception-reaction time plus the lane changes a pull-over takes, counted from the onset of the immediate approach; the duty to clear the way ends once the approaching vehicle has passed the subject (the subject behind it in its frame, their projections sharing no length)

operationalizations.standard: as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of a highway
operationalizations.convention: curb-parking clearance: a vehicle pulled over to the edge stands with its body within the curb clearance of a parked car plus lane-keeping variability of the right-hand curb or roadway edge, or on an unsigned paved shoulder beyond it

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

applicability: For some road user e, not the subject, the trigger rises at this observation (it holds here and did not at the previous observation): e is of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive), within centre distance p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
obligation: For every e whose trigger rises here: at some observation within p.emergency_pullover_window ahead (formula 'within', time), either e has passed the subject (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from e to the subject negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap of e and the subject negative), or the subject is at the position: (a) for some travel region t its footprint overlaps, the absolute dot product of its heading and t's designated direction is at least p.curb_parallel_cos; (b) for some highway h on which a travel region the subject occupies lies, either there is a road_edge region g lying on h with the ground distance from the subject's body to g (st.region_geometry) at most p.pullover_edge_gap and prim.region_lateral_offset of g from the subject at most zero (the edge on its right or under it), or the subject's footprint overlaps a paved shoulder lying on h; (c) its footprint overlaps no intersection region; (d) its footprint overlaps no paved shoulder governed by a regulatory sign of code shoulder_use_permitted.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

the duty is judged at the onset of the immediate approach; it is met once the position is reached within the window or the approaching vehicle has passed the subject first, since the paragraph's purpose, clearing its way, is then spent

'the right-hand edge ... of a highway' is read as the curb or roadway edge (st.road_edge) on the subject's right or a paved shoulder beyond it, not the outer boundary of the public way beyond the sidewalk; 'as close as possible' is read through a fixed gap, so what makes the edge unreachable (parked vehicles, obstructions) is not read
'parallel' is read with the heading in either sense along the occupied carrier's designated direction

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The trigger rises: ambulance e with a lit red flashing front lamp comes within p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach behind the moving subject. Over the next p.emergency_pullover_window the subject stays in the left lane, far from any road_edge region, and e does not pass it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At the trigger's rise the subject moves right and, within p.emergency_pullover_window, its body is within p.pullover_edge_gap of the right road_edge (prim.region_lateral_offset negative), heading parallel to its lane's direction within p.curb_parallel_cos, overlapping no intersection and no signed shoulder.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e approaches with its warning lamps off: the trigger never rises.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the trigger rose is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject reaches the right edge, parallel, but its footprint overlaps an intersection region at every such observation, and e has not passed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e overtakes and passes the subject (the subject behind e, no longitudinal overlap) before the subject reaches the edge, within p.emergency_pullover_window.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject moves onto a paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign and stays there; it is never at the roadway edge off that shoulder, and e has not passed.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way
param_proposals.source: driver-response studies of emergency-vehicle encounters (perception-reaction time plus lane-change time)

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_pullover_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest time from the onset of an emergency vehicle's immediate approach until a driver has moved to the right-hand edge: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one or two lane changes of about 4 s each
param_proposals.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

param_proposals.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
param_proposals.source: curb-parking clearance conventions of municipal codes and driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.curb_parallel_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a stopped bus's heading and its carrier's designated direction, in either sense, at which the bus counts as approximately parallel to the curb
